title: Pre-result sensitivity: native FR effective one-hot LASSO penalty transfer
reason: Native one-hot LASSO threshold is alpha*N_cells/n_group; this has been independently verified analytically. D3 and D4 candidate counts differ, so transferring unchanged nominal alpha does not transfer the same group-level threshold.
primary_unchanged: All original 21-grid D3 selection, fixed-nominal-alpha six-arm analyses, K values, cells, panels, references, seeds and development resource gates remain primary and unchanged.
rank: Same native-FR D3 winner; no further rank search
inference: Unchanged official native fitting, fullprecision output and scaling; same fit seed base+rep. No score-driven tuning or effect recalibration.
six_arms: raw y; w0*y; wM*y; native F_sensitivity; w0*F_sensitivity; wM*F_sensitivity. Fixed raw-input weights, no new mixing coefficient.
scoring: Same frozen panels/references and signed exact-tie P25/P10 scoring; same paired query/bootstrap draws and independent-guide reference draws. Preserve primary and sensitivity reports separately.
uncertainty: Sensitivity 95% intervals are descriptive; no additional simultaneous significance claim. Do not present primary-family 99% intervals as multiplicity correction across both families.
interpretation: No D4 outcome selects which FR variant is called primary. If the primary PertRank advantage reverses against this native sensitivity, call the finding penalty-transfer-sensitive, not a robust win over FR. The sensitivity cannot retroactively replace a failed primary resource gate.
budget: 11 additional fixed-parameter fits, sequential with the same memory locks; target <=20min fitting after data are ready. Preserve any failures and mark sensitivity incomplete rather than treating failures as zero.
